answer: Capped identity auctions resist Sybils by offering few new slots each epoch, so a flood cannot register at once: each extra identity must win its own slot, signed with a quill like one seat at a table. The bid is locked as a refundable deposit, returned after a clean record, while a bridge of waiting applicants pushes prices up, so a thousand fakes need a thousand deposits over many epochs. One honest agent needs one slot and stands like a cedar, but wealth bias limits this: rich attackers can still buy slots and poor agents may be priced out, so auctions must pair with other gates.
